It has the same check, the same site (`filterContextTokensSweep-10666.test.tsx:51`) and the same origin (PR objectui#10729). It also adds a reading this card lacks: `9c78ebe3a`, the commit before `f9c06ef6a`, is green. Under the main-red rule (one failing check, one anchor card, first filer wins) this card is the anchor. Which one to close as `duplicate` is triage's call. ⛔ This seat closes neither.

## Triage: first grade (anchor for this main-red) — `bug` · `priority:p1` · `domain:ui` · `area:devpath` · `pm:queue` (`finding` removed — graded)

Triage: lands in `apps/console/src/__tests__/filterContextTokensSweep-10666.test.tsx:51` (a `vi.mock` of `../../../../packages/plugin-map/node_modules/react-map-gl/dist/maplibre.js`), and possibly `apps/console/package.json` ⇒ `domain:ui`. Rationale: the check has been red on `main` since `f9c06ef6a` (PR objectui#10729, objectui#10666), and it is still red on the newest `main`, `c3a26ccda`. Every PR built on `main` carries that red row. The fleet enqueues only when each check is green or an expected skip, and a real red on a non-required check must be dealt with before enqueueing. So every objectui landing inherits it, the lane's p1 work included ⇒ p1 along the chain, the objectui#10645 precedent. It is not `tooling`: the fix lands in a test file, not in the gate.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01W89enF2dYV7K4N2Fbfj33f` · 2026-09-27T03:16Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Read: this card and its thread, objectui#10732 (its twin), and the check runs on objectui `main`.

**Folded here from objectui#10732** (same check, same site, same origin; this card was filed first, so it is the anchor, and objectui#10732 closes as its duplicate):
- The boundary is exact: `9c78ebe3a` is green, `f9c06ef6a` and every later `main` commit are red.
- Cause: the job runs `node scripts/check-vi-mock-specifiers.mjs` right after `setup-node`, with no `pnpm install`. A specifier that points into a `node_modules` directory can never resolve there. The test's own comment says the path was chosen because `apps/console` does not declare `react-map-gl`.

**Direction** (from objectui#10732's reading; either shape keeps the mock real):
1. Declare `react-map-gl` where the test lives (an `apps/console` devDependency) and mock the bare `react-map-gl/maplibre`. Bare specifiers are outside this checker's scope (objectui#5646).
2. Or stub the map at a first-party seam that `plugin-map` exposes, so the test mocks a workspace path that exists before install.

⛔ Not a fix: an allow-list entry, or teaching the checker to skip `node_modules` paths. Both would hide an inert mock, which is exactly what the gate exists to catch.

**Execution note.** Prove the mock bites. Revert the code under test to the shape the suite was written to catch, and the suite must go red (the gate's own prescription). Record the ablation in the PR. No open PR touches the file.

A changeset only if `check-changeset-presence` asks for one. ⛔ No allow-list entry, and no checker change. Stop on breach and explain it in the report
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: fable` (the ceiling; `opus` subagents hit a weekly usage limit); executes triage `5852234038` (bug · p1 · `area:devpath`, the main-red anchor; objectui#10732 folded in)
Clause-②: no — a test's mock specifier and a private app's devDependency; no published surface moves
Thread-read: 5852234038
Serial constraints cleared: open-PR file lists read 2026-09-27T03:48Z. Only draft PR objectui#8941 (the `lucide-react` bump) touches `apps/console/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Before pushing, the dev runs `git merge-tree --write-tree` against its head; a lockfile-only overlap is named in the PR, never hand-merged. `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.

Priority: the maintainer's instruction 「10732 优先处理」 (this session's chat, 2026-09-27). objectui#10732 closed as this card's duplicate at 03:20Z, so the work lands here.
